name: Chalcedony Yellow
lede: Chalcedony Yellow is a pale, greenish yellow named for chalcedony, a waxy mineral used in beads and carvings, and recorded by Ridgway in 1912.

sections.title: A mineral's pale yellow
sections.body:
Our library traces Chalcedony Yellow to chalcedony, a translucent form of quartz long carved into beads, seals and cameos, with Ridgway's 1912 standards placing it on plate XVII, hue 25′, tone b [1]. Maerz and Paul separately date a close match to 1912 as well, on plate 10 I 1 of their 1930 dictionary, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system would class it as light greenish yellow, 3.8 units of ΔE away [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[straw]], [[sandy]], [[light-chalcedony-yellow]] and [[primrose-yellow]], at 2.8, 3.1, 3.9 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. In LCH terms it is light and fairly saturated: lightness 85, chroma 46, hue 99 degrees [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Chalcedony Yellow in 141, about 0.6 percent, as photographed [2]. Its earliest appearance is Fra Angelico's *Coronation of the Virgin*, from about 1434, and its fullest is an undated Indian painting of the snake goddess Manasa, where it covers about 69 percent of the canvas [2]. Its use across the archive is markedly higher in paintings from India, 5.2 times the rate expected by chance, and peaks in a cluster of works from the 1890s [2].
